facts.raw_span: a 3-year history of slowly progressive lower urinary tract symptoms
nocturia two to three times per night
a slow urinary stream
Urinalysis showed microscopic hematuria (3–5 red cells per high-power field)
no history of lichen sclerosis
no history of sexually transmitted infection
Renal ultrasonography findings were normal
Flexible cystourethroscopy revealed a circumferential urethral mass
biopsy specimens were negative for carcinoma
biopsy specimens demonstrated amyloid protein deposition
Retrograde urethrography showed an approximately 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra
no palpable induration along the ventral penile shaft

concepts.why: The presence of a urethral mass with biopsy-proven amyloid protein deposition and a segment of stenosis in the penile urethra supports this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of slow urinary stream and the finding of a 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra on retrograde urethrography support this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of slowly progressive lower urinary tract symptoms, including nocturia and microscopic hematuria, could be explained by chronic urethritis.

Although biopsy specimens were negative for carcinoma, the initial finding of a circumferential urethral mass raised concern for urothelial carcinoma, and this diagnosis cannot be entirely ruled out without further evaluation.

The presence of amyloid protein deposition in the urethral biopsy specimens suggests the possibility of systemic amyloidosis, although the patient's systemic evaluation did not reveal additional disease manifestations.
The biopsy specimens were negative for carcinoma but demonstrated amyloid protein deposition, which explains the presence of amyloidosis in the urethra.

rationales.F08: Circumferential urethral mass is concerning for urethral carcinoma or amyloidosis
rationales.F09: Biopsy negative for carcinoma reduces likelihood of urethral carcinoma
rationales.F10: Amyloid protein deposition in biopsy specimens is diagnostic for amyloidosis
rationales.F11: Urethral stenosis is a common cause of lower urinary tract symptoms

frontier_selector.rationale: Biopsy specimens demonstrated amyloid protein deposition and the presence of a circumferential urethral mass, which are specific findings that support Primary Amyloidosis of the Urethra, while Urethral Stenosis is also considered due to the patient's symptoms and retrograde urethrography results.
